name: Exec

intent.description: Human-readable summary of what these commands do, so the user can understand the intent at a glance.

commands.description: Commands to execute. A single command runs directly; two or more commands are connected as a pipeline (stdout → stdin).

program.description: The program, binary, or script path to execute. Supports ~ and $VAR expansion. Must be on $PATH or an absolute path — no shell expansion of globs or operators.

args.description: Arguments to the program. Each argument is a separate string — no shell quoting or escaping needed. Note: ~ and $VAR are NOT expanded in args. Use absolute paths or let the program resolve them.

stdin.description: Content to pipe to stdin. Use instead of heredocs.

path.description: File path to redirect output to. Supports ~ and $VAR expansion.

append.description: Append to file instead of overwriting

cwd.description: Working directory for this command. Supports ~ and $VAR expansion.

env.description: Environment variables to set for this command.

merge_stderr.description: Merge stderr into stdout (equivalent to 2>&1). Combined output appears in stdout; stderr will be empty.

chaining.description: sequential: run all (;). bail_on_error: stop on first failure (&&). independent: run all, report each.

stripAnsi.description: Strip ANSI escape codes from output (default: true). Set false to preserve raw color/formatting codes.

input_examples.intent: Run tests in a specific package
